statement.text:
Suppose that A and G are finite groups such that A acts coprimely on G by
automorphisms. Let C = CG (A) be the fixed-point subgroup, and let C ′ denote its
derived subgroup.
    Is it true that the number of A-invariant irreducible characters χ of G whose
restriction χC is never zero is exactly |C/C ′ |? This would follow if one could show
that χC is never zero if and only if the Glauberman–Isaacs correspondent χ∗ of χ is
linear.                                                                    G. Navarro
